items.title: Empire State Building Lit Up with Gold Marks Historic Milestone of NASA’s Voyager 1 This Week
lines: Did you see Voyager 1 is now one full light day away from Earth?
Wait, so a signal takes a whole day to get back?
Yep, 24 hours. And the Empire State Building lit up gold to celebrate.

items.title: Bizarre deep-sea fish with a see-through head captured in stunning 4K
lines: Apparently there is a fish with a see through head, called the barreleye.
That sounds made up. Where does it even live?
Nearly 2,000 feet down, and its eyes rotate forward to chase prey.

items.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
lines: I just read that crows make visual decisions twice as fast as humans.
So the crows outside are judging us at double speed?
About 235 milliseconds on average. Faster than me picking a coffee.

items.title: This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history
lines: There was a whale 6 million years ago with a super crooked face.
Possibly the most lopsided mammal ever. Found in Peru, of all places.

items.title: Scientists discover a giant 66-pound rodent that lived 34 million years ago
lines: Scientists found a rodent in Thailand that weighed around 66 pounds.
That is not a mouse, that is a roommate.
And it lived 34 million years ago. Good luck fitting that in a trap.
